description: Use this when the user wants a timeline chart, a chronology or a history graphic from dated events, with a file to download. Places events to scale by day count (or at even gaps), stacks labels in rows so they do not overlap, draws spans as bars and eras as bands, and returns SVG, PDF (Letter or A4) and CSV links. Reads YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, month names and BC years. Up to 200 events and 20 eras. Does not convert Julian calendar dates, does not research dates, and refuses ambiguous slashed dates unless date_order is given. Do not use for project schedules with task dependencies.

date_order.description: Only for slashed dates such as 03/04/2025: month_first reads March 4, day_first reads 3 April. Without it such dates are refused as ambiguous.

events.description: 1 to 200 events in any order, e.g. [{"date":"1957-10-04","label":"Sputnik 1"},{"date":"1969-07-20","label":"Moon landing"}].

category.description: Optional group used for color and the filter, e.g. "Space".

date.description: When it happened: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD, a month name ("July 1969", "20 July 1969"), or a BC year ("500 BC" or -500). "c. 1500" marks an approximate date. Example: "1969-07-20".

detail.description: Optional note shown when the event is clicked and in the CSV, e.g. "Apollo 11, Armstrong and Aldrin".

end_date.description: Last date for a span such as a war or a reign, same formats as date. A year means the whole year. Example: "1945".

label.description: Short event name shown on the chart, e.g. "Moon landing".

orientation.description: horizontal (default, landscape PDF) or vertical (time runs down the page, portrait PDF). Vertical suits long lists.

page_size.description: PDF paper size: letter (default) or a4.

periods.description: Optional eras drawn as shaded bands along the axis (up to 20), e.g. [{"label":"Cold War","start":"1947","end":"1991"}].

end.description: Last date of the era, e.g. "1991".

label.description: Era or phase name, e.g. "Cold War".

start.description: First date of the era, same formats as event dates, e.g. "1947".

scale.description: to_scale (default) places each date by its day count, so gaps are true to time. even puts events at equal gaps in date order.

name: generate_timeline
title: Generate timeline
